models.name: A-LEAF (Arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian FSI)
models.what_it_computes: Transient coaptation area fraction and maximum principal stress on leaflets using ALE Navier–Stokes coupled to anisotropic hyperelastic shells

models.name: E-VALVE (Embedded-boundary FSI)
models.what_it_computes: Leaflet coaptation metric and peak principal stress using an immersed-boundary flow solver coupled to thin-shell finite elements

models.name: PULSE (Partitioned ROM–CFD–FEM)
models.what_it_computes: Coaptation area fraction and peak leaflet stress via a partitioned solver coupling a reduced-order inflow circuit, incompressible CFD, and nonlinear shells

mechanisms.name: Diastolic sealing
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Sustained coaptation under physiologic afterload prevents regurgitation; stresses during closure influence durability.

mechanisms.name: Peak systolic opening
mechanisms.why_it_matters: High flow rates and leaflet curvature determine stress levels linked to fatigue and material damage.

mechanisms.name: Rapid closure water-hammer
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Transient pressure reversal during deceleration produces short-duration stress spikes associated with early tears.

deviation.detail: Throughout, the 'Model inputs' credibility factor is referred to as the 'Input Realism Index (IRI)' and scored under that name.

spans: DICinferred peak principal stress during middiastole was 0.83 MPa (95% CI: 0.79–0.87 MPa); ALEAF predicted 0.91 MPa, a 9.4% difference.
